_doc: A2.5: respuestas de fallo en la voz de Dex (src/systems/FailResponses.ts). Todo literal, sin {item} ni ${…}: cada frase tiene clip (scripts/voices/extract.mjs, hablante player). Lo de cada hotspot/NPC va en su scene.json (useResponses). Linter: regla j.

LOOK: I look at it. It looks back. Neither of us learns anything.
Nothing jumps out. Which is exactly what a clue would want me to think.
I stare at it for a while. Patience, they said. Still nothing.
Perfectly ordinary. Suspiciously ordinary. No. Just ordinary.
USE: I poke at it. It doesn't do anything. I respect the commitment.
I try using it. Nothing. Some things just exist, Dex.
No obvious way to use that. And I've tried the non-obvious ones too.
I give it a firm, professional nudge. It remains unbothered.
TALK: I say hello. It says nothing. Honestly, a better listener than most of my followers.
I clear my throat and wait. It doesn't want to talk. Detectives get that a lot.
'Seen anything suspicious lately?' Silence. Classic witness.
PICK: I'd love to take it. It would love to stay. It wins.
That's not coming with me. My pockets have standards. Low ones, but still.
I try to pick it up. It's very attached to where it is.
Not pocket-sized. Not pocket-shaped. Not happening.
OPEN: It doesn't open. A closed case. I'd recognise one, if I'd ever closed one.
No lid, no door, no hinge. Nothing to open here but my mind.
I look for a way to open it. It's a very private object.
CLOSE: It's not open. I can't close what isn't open. That's just philosophy.
Nothing to close here. Closing things isn't my strong suit anyway. Ask my case files.
I try to close it. It's already as closed as it gets.
PUSH: I push it. It doesn't move. I feel pushed back, emotionally.
I lean on it with my full weight. My full weight is not enough.
I give it a shove. It holds. Strong support level. ...It's just heavy, Dex.
PULL: I pull. It doesn't budge. My lower back files a complaint.
I tug at it. Nothing comes loose except my dignity.
I yank it. It stays exactly where it was. Respect.
GIVE: Give it to whom? It's not a person. I checked.
I hold out my hand to it. Nobody takes anything. Awkward for both of us.
There's nobody here to give anything to. I'll save my generosity for later.

LOOK: I turn it over in my hands. It's exactly what it looks like.
I squint at it. My 3D glasses add nothing. They never do.
I examine it closely. Same as before. Reassuring, in a way.
OPEN: I don't think I can open this.
I check for a hidden compartment. None. Adrian didn't think of everything.
I try to open it. It's not that kind of thing. Most things aren't.
CLOSE: Not the kind of thing you close.
It's already as closed as a pocket thing can be.
I close my hand around it. That's as much closing as it gets.
PUSH: I push it around in my pocket. Thrilling.
I press on it. It doesn't click, beep or confess.
I nudge it. Still in my pocket. Mission accomplished, I guess.
PULL: I tug on it. Nothing happens. As expected.
I pull it out, stare at it, put it back. Detective work.
I give it a pull. It doesn't unfold into a clue.
TALK: I hold it to my ear. Silence. It's not a seashell.
'Talk to me.' It doesn't. Witnesses never do.
I ask it where Patient Zero is. It plays dumb. Very convincing.
GIVE: Nobody here to give it to.
I offer it to the empty air. The air politely declines.
I'd give it away, but there's nobody around to impress.
PICK: Already in my inventory. Mission accomplished.
I already have it. Picking it up twice doesn't make two.
It's in my pocket. I check twice. Still there.

itemHotspot: That doesn't go there. I can feel it. Mostly in my ego.
I try it. Nothing happens. Bold idea, though.
Wrong tool, wrong place. Story of my career.
I press the two together. Neither of them is impressed.
Not like that. Not even close. Probably.

USE: I wave it at them. They wait for me to stop. I stop.
They look at it, then at me. Mostly at me. Not kindly.
Using things on people. Not my finest investigative technique.
GIVE: They don't want it. I can tell. People make a face.
I hold it out. They hold out nothing. A clear no.
'No thanks,' says their face. Their face is very articulate.

default: I rub them together. No sparks. No magic. Just friction.
Those two don't go together. Like me and early nights.
I try combining them. They refuse to be a team.
Nothing happens. In my head it was brilliant.
I mash them together. My pockets disapprove.
Not a combo. Not even a cute accident. Next.

lines: I nail the half note to the plank. Now it's a tiny protest sign. 'GIVE ME THE OTHER HALF.' I take it back off.
I hold the foil scrap on the end of the plank like a flag. A flag that says 14. Nobody salutes.
I check if the Ledger PIN is 73. It isn't. Adrian isn't that careless. Only with doors.
I hold the code against the keycard. Numbers on a card. They don't merge. The keypad wants the note, not the card.
I try to back up the Ledger onto the floppy. One point four four megabytes. My trust issues alone are bigger.
I read the printout through the 3D glasses. The map pops out. Slightly. Not helpfully.
Pepe already wears tiny 3D glasses. A second pair would just be showing off.
Spring water and BULL RUN. A balanced diet. I'm not mixing them. I'm not a monster.
I'm not pouring water on a burned chip. Water and chips are how it got burned. Probably.
I press the golden token against the Ledger. It doesn't absorb it. It's a hardware wallet, not a piggy bank.
A keycard and a key fob. Two keys, no door. I'm basically a janitor.
I put the 3D glasses on the duck. He looks like an influencer. I take them back before he gets a following.
I hold the antenna to the Ledger. More bars. Same balance.
I tuck the code into the envelope. Now it's a mystery with a spoiler. I take it back out.
Two notes, two handwritings, one theme: everybody knew something except me.
A vet bill and a hardware wallet. Gerald isn't covered. Nothing here is covered.
7314 and a duck. If that's Adrian's whole security model, I'm already in. ...I'm not already in.
They came out of the mailbox together. I'm not putting them back together. They've had enough.
I could forge a new seal with the pen. Penny already resealed it. Badly. Two bad seals don't make a good one.
I'm not writing on Gerald's medical records. Blue ink would upset him. He's yellow.
I try to doodle a moustache on Adrian's keycard photo. The pen leaks a beard instead. I wipe it off. Mostly.
Grease on the keycard. The reader would never trust me again. Readers hold grudges.
I'm not greasing the terminal key. It already slides into things just fine.
Pizza and an energy drink. The full Adrian. I'm not ready for the full Adrian.
The plank got the Ledger out. The Ledger doesn't owe it anything. That's not how leverage works.

printout: I hold the printout up to it. No match. The map is of somewhere else.
I compare them. The printout disagrees. The printout usually wins.
I'm not wasting fading thermal paper on that. It's my only map.
floppy_disk: I look for a floppy slot. There isn't one. It's not 1997 in here.
I'm not sliding my BACKUP into random things. That's how backups die.
I tap the floppy on it. Nothing loads. Nothing ever loads first try.
monkey_sticker: I almost stick the monkey on it. Then I picture all three heads judging me.
The sticker would look great there. That's not a clue. That's decorating.
A three-headed monkey won't solve that. It would make it funnier.
broken_mouse: I click the broken mouse at it. It doesn't click back. It's done clicking.
Wrong kind of mouse for this. Also, the wrong kind of working.
I dangle the mouse by its cable over it. A sad little pendulum. Nothing else.
sign_in_sheet: I hold the sign-in sheet up to it. Nobody on the list matches. Not even it.
I'm not signing that in. It's not a patient. I think.
The sheet flutters uselessly. Those diagnoses are wasted on furniture.
clinic_note: I show it Dr. Satoshi's note. It doesn't care about Day 47. Nobody did. That's the sad part.
I smooth the note out against it. Still crumpled. Still sad.
It's a note, not a key. Even if it reads like a confession.
clinic_sign_in_sheet: I wave the clinic's sign-in sheet at it. It doesn't sign in.
No pen, no patient, no point. The sheet stays with me.
I check whether it's on the clinic's list. It isn't. Lucky it.
clinic_photo: I hold the old photo next to it. Happier times for the photo. Same times for this.
I compare the grand opening photo with this. Things were tidier back then. Everything was.
It's evidence, not a bookmark. The photo stays with me.
dr_satoshi_badge: I flash the badge at it. It doesn't salute. Rude, for a medical facility.
'Doctor coming through.' Nothing comes through. Including me.
Out here the badge has the authority of a sticky note. Possibly less.
keycard: I swipe the keycard over it. No reader. Just me, swiping air like an idiot.
No slot, no beep. The card goes back in my pocket, where it's appreciated.
I tap the card on it. Adrian's photo stares back, disappointed.
vip_floppy: The VIP floppy is too exclusive for that. It has a velvet rope. A metaphorical one.
I look for a slot. No slot. VIP access denied by geometry.
I'm not wasting the VIP disc on that. It's VIP. I'm barely P.
golden_token: I look for a slot to drop the token in. There's no slot. There's never a slot.
I tap the golden token on it. It rings. Nothing opens. Lovely ring, though.
It's the shiniest thing I own. It's not going in there.
pepememe: I show it the Rare Pepe. It doesn't get it. Normies.
The Pepe is too rare for this. It's a specimen, not a spatula.
I hold up Pepe. Pepe holds up his tiny 3D glasses. Nothing happens. Classic Pepe.
water_bottle: I splash a little water on it. Now it's wet. That's the whole result.
I'm saving this water. Something around here is thirsty. I can feel it.
Pouring mountain water on that would be a waste. Of the water, and of the hike.
code_note: I hold 7314 up to it. No keypad. Numbers are useless without buttons.
I read the code to it. 'Seven. Three. One. Four.' It isn't listening.
The code goes in a keypad. That isn't a keypad. Even I can see that.
mystery_envelope: I'm not posting the envelope into that. It's CONFIDENTIAL. It says so. In capitals.
I wave the envelope at it. Confidential things don't like being waved.
The envelope stays sealed and stays with me. Somebody around here would love to read it.
mystery_envelope_opened: The torn envelope has nothing left to give. Unlike me. I'm full of gifts.
I wave the empty envelope at it. Empty gestures. My speciality.
It's an envelope with a hole in it. It doesn't open anything else.
ledger: I look for a USB port. No port. The Ledger stays unplugged and smug.
I hold the Ledger up to it. The screen says nothing. Hardware wallets are very discreet.
Not your keys, not your coins. Not your port, not my problem.
rubber_duck: I squeak the duck at it. It doesn't squeak back. No sense of humour.
I set the duck on it, then take him back. He didn't like it there.
The duck looks at it, then at me. Even the duck knows that's not it.
antenna: I poke it with the antenna. Two bars. Zero results.
I wave the antenna around. I pick up a faint radio station and no clues.
I tap it with the antenna. Tink. Not the useful kind of tink.
burned_chip: I hold the burned chip to it. Smells like ambition. Does nothing.
That chip already gave everything it had. Let it rest.
I'm not sticking a scorched chip in that. One fire per day.
server_log: I read the server log to it. Error, error, timeout. It doesn't care either.
I slap the log against it. Paperwork never solved anything. Except crimes.
Logs explain what went wrong. They don't fix it. Story of the internet.
glasses_3d: I look at it through the spare 3D glasses. It's still there. Now in red and cyan.
I hold the spare glasses up to it. It doesn't need a second opinion.
Two pairs of 3D glasses on one detective. Still nothing. My eyes file a complaint.
adrian_note: I'm not using Adrian's note as a tool. It's the only thing he left me in person.
I hold the note against it. The handwriting doesn't change. Neither does that.
Adrian's note stays folded. Some paper is for reading, not for poking.
terminal_key: I look for a keyhole. No keyhole. The fob blinks green anyway. Very supportive.
I press the key fob against it. The LED blinks. Nothing else does.
Wrong terminal. Wrong everything. The fob blinks politely.
energy_drink: I'm not pouring BULL RUN on that. It's not that tired.
I offer it the energy drink. It's an object. It runs on zero energy. Admirable.
Five hundred milligrams of caffeine, wasted on that? Something around here needs it more.
receipt: I hold the receipt up to it. 'One BTC at three fifty.' It looks sad too.
A receipt is proof that something happened. Nothing is happening here.
I'm not wiping anything with this. It's a historical document of pain.
ape_costume: I drape the ape costume over it. It doesn't fit. I take it back before anyone sees.
The costume is for wearing, not for rubbing on things. I've been told.
I hold the ape costume against it. Bad fit. The costume prefers me.
luxury_watch: I tap the watch on it. Tick. Tick. Nothing. Time isn't the problem here.
I'm not scratching a watch that expensive on that.
I check the watch instead. It's wrong-idea o'clock.
floppy_box: No drive here. The holographic floppies glow at it anyway. Showing off.
I'm not wasting an AdrianLAB floppy on that. They need a computer. A real one.
I hold up the box of floppies. It rattles. Nothing loads. Still beautiful.
patient_file: The file's seal stays on. Not on that. Not today.
I'm not breaking Patient Zero's seal against that. This needs a proper desk.
'PATIENT ZERO', in red. It deserves better than being rubbed on things.
note_half_a: Two digits won't open that. Two digits barely open a conversation.
I hold up the 73. Nothing happens. Half a clue does half of nothing.
Not there. The other half is with the birds. That's where this is going.
note_half_b: I wave the foil scrap at it. Shiny. Useless. The magpies would be proud.
Fourteen. On its own it's just a number. Like my follower count, minus the bots.
Half a code. It needs its other half before it's good for anything. Relatable.
fence_plank: I poke it with the plank. It doesn't fall. Not everything is a nest.
I'm not hitting that with a plank. I'm a detective. Mostly.
The plank is long. That isn't high, low or stuck. Wrong job for a plank.
vet_bill: I wave the vet bill at it. Gerald's clean bill of health impresses nobody but me.
Not a vet thing. Gerald's paperwork stays in my pocket, where confidential things go.
I hold up the bill. 'Diagnosis: perfect.' That's Gerald's. This isn't.
leaky_pen: I try the pen on it. Blue drips everywhere. Nothing gets signed, everything gets stained.
Not the right time for the pen. It leaks anyway. It doesn't care about timing.
I hold the pen over it. A drop falls. I watch it fall. That's the whole plan, apparently.
pizza_slice: I rub the slice on it. Now it's greasy and still useless. Grease isn't magic. Mostly.
This doesn't need lubricant. Something on this building does. Something rusty.
I hold the slice up to it. A drop of grease falls. Nothing else happens. Nothing ever does.
empty_can: I offer it the empty can. It's empty. So is the gesture.
Nothing comes out. Something around here wants it full. Of something.
I tap the can on it. Hollow sound. Same as my portfolio.
rainwater_can: I'm not wasting good rain on that. Someone in this building only drinks rain.
I hold the can over it. A drop falls. Nothing grows. Wrong customer.
That doesn't need watering. Something green downstairs does.
extension_cord: I offer it the cord. It has nothing to plug in. Neither do I, emotionally.
Not everything needs power. This, apparently, doesn't. Rare.
I wave the extension cord at it. One metre short of a plan.
scrap_paper: I hold up the blank paper. It says nothing. It agrees with everything.
Blank paper won't help here. Written paper might. Different paper.
I press the scrap against it. Now it's a scrap pressed against a thing.
fake_alpha: I show it my alpha. 'BUY $GERALD.' It doesn't buy it. It's not a bot.
This alpha has one target audience, and it's not this.
I wave the fake alpha around. Nothing in this room is gullible enough. Yet.
marked_map: I check the map against it. The X isn't here. The X is up the mountain.
The map is for the mountain, not for this.
I unfold the map. It points the other way. Outside. Up.
patient_wristband: I flash my wristband at it. It is unimpressed by my diagnosis.
The wristband says I'm a patient. Not that I'm useful.
I hold up my wrist. Nobody here checks bracelets but the clinic.
sobriety_chip: The sobriety chip does nothing here. Sobriety rarely does.
I offer the chip. Worth nothing. It agrees.
This token is for the doctor. He collects them.
